2023 (earlier Section 439 Cr.P.C.), for grant of regular bail to the petitioners, during the pendency of trial, who have been booked in a criminal case arising out of First Information Report, as detailed hereunder:-

FIR has been registered at the instance of complainant Rahul with the allegation that he is 10+2 passed and a student of B.A.(3rd year).
Apart this, he is a national level wrestler and used to participate in wrestling tournaments.

During which period, he came into contact with petitioners,
namely; Kuldeep and Arjun, and in July 2023, they made him to meet other co-accused, namely,
Surender and Atul Jain and told that both of them are able to provide employment to unemployed persons in Indian Agriculture Research Institute, New Delhi.

entities.text: Indian Agriculture Research Institute, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On being allured by them for getting the employment as Clerk, he had paid an amount Rs. 10 lakhs.
Details of the payments made on several occasions in the year 2023 have been mentioned in the FIR.
Thereafter, complainant was handed over a fake joining letter/appointment letter.
Neither the amount was paid back, nor the actual appointment letter was ever given to the complainant, from the accused persons.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners argues that other co- accused Deepak Kumar, has been extended the concession of anticipatory bail by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 09.12.2024 vide CRM-M-61527-2024 (Annexure P-2).

Further submits that age of 2 of 4 CRM-M-43782-2025 (O&M) -3- petitioner Kuldeep is about 37 years, he is behind the bars since 20.12.2024 and Arjun is about 35 years, he is behind the bars since 25.01.2025.
There being no truthfulness in the allegations, unless the trial is culminated finally and liberty of petitioners cannot be curtailed by detaining them for indefinite period.
Thus, prays for grant of regular bail.

5. On the other hand, learned Sr. DAG Punjab, Mr. Pawan Kumar Jhanda argues that investigation has been completed and challan has also been submitted, though, charges are yet to be framed and thereupon list of total 26 prosecution witnesses has to be exhausted.
He does not dispute that all the offences are triable by the Court of learned Magistrate.
6. I have considered the submissions addressed by learned counsel from both the sides and also examined the record alongwith the appended documents.
All the offences are triable by the Court of learned Magistrate.

Both the petitioners, namely, Kuldeep (in CRM-M-43782- 2025) and Arjun (in CRM-M-49355-2025) are inside the jail since 20.12.2024 and 25.01.2025 respectively and their any longer incarceration is not going to serve any meaningful purpose, to the prosecution or to any other urgency for just decision of the trial.
7. Truthfulness in the allegations and also as to whether there was any fault of the complainant, who attempted to secure job by paying money is yet to be ascertained by the trial Court.
8. Accordingly, the petitions are allowed.

Petitioners are ordered to be released on bail, subject to their furnishing bail/surety 3 of 4 CRM-M-43782-2025 (O&M) -4- bonds to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court/ Chief Judicial Magistrate/ Illaqa Magistrate/ Duty Magistrate concerned, if not required in any other case.
